   303	
   304	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   305	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   306	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   307	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   309	-/
   310	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   311	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   312	
   313	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   314	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   315	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   316	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   317	-/
   318	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   319	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   320	  simp [pauliEdges]
   321	
   322	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   323	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   324	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   325	-/
   326	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   327	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   328	  by
   329	    classical
   330	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   331	    exact
   332	      Distribution.map
   333	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   334	        (fun s =>
   335	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   336	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   337	
   338	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   339	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   340	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   341	-/
   342	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   343	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   344	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   345	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   346	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   347	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   348	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   349	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   350	  deriving DecidableEq
   351	
   352	/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Pauli-test answer
   353	alphabet to a Pauli register. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a
   354	Pauli question yields a complete `PauliRegister`-indexed measurement. -/
   355	def pauliAnswerOrZero {P : AdmissibleParams} : PauliAnswer P → PauliRegister P
   356	  | .pauliOutcome u => u
   357	  | _ => 0
   358	
   359	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   360	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   361	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   362	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   363	-/
   364	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   365	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   366	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   367	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   368	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   369	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   370	
   371	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   372	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   373	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   374	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   375	-/
   376	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   377	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   378	  toFun
   379	    | .value a => .inl a
   380	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   381	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   382	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   383	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   384	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   385	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   386	  invFun
   387	    | .inl a => .value a
   388	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   389	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   390	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   391	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   392	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   393	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   394	  left_inv := by
   395	    intro x
   396	    cases x <;> rfl
   397	  right_inv := by
   398	    intro x
   399	    cases x with
   400	    | inl a => rfl
   401	    | inr x =>
   402	        cases x with
   403	        | inl a => rfl
   404	        | inr x =>
   405	            cases x with
   406	            | inl a => rfl
   407	            | inr x =>
   408	                cases x with
   409	                | inl a => rfl
   410	                | inr x =>
   411	                    cases x with
   412	                    | inl a => rfl
   413	                    | inr x =>
   414	                        cases x with
   415	                        | inl a => rfl
   416	                        | inr a => rfl
   417	
   418	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   419	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
   420	
   421	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   422	  ⟨.bit 0⟩
   423	
   424	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   425	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   426	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   427	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   428	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   429	-/
   430	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   431	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   432	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   434	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   435	
   436	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   437	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   440	-/
   441	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   442	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   443	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   444	
   445	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   446	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   447	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   448	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   449	-/
   450	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   451	  match t, a with
   452	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   453	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   454	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   455	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   456	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   457	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   458	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   459	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   460	  | _, _ => false
   461	
   462	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   470	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   471	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   472	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   473	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   474	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   475	
   476	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   477	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   478	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   479	-/
   480	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   481	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   482	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   483	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   484	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   485	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   486	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   487	
   488	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   489	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   490	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   491	-/
   492	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   493	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   494	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   495	
   496	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   497	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   498	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   499	-/
   500	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   501	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   502	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   503	    (match W with
   504	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   505	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   506	
   507	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   508	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   514	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   515	      (a * (match W with
   516	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   517	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   518	
   519	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   520	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   521	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   522	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   523	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   524	-/
   525	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   526	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   527	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   528	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   529	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   530	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   531	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   532	
   533	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   534	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   535	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   536	-/
   537	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   538	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   539	  open Classical in
   540	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   541	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   542	      if tA = tB then
   543	        decide (a = b)
   544	      else
   545	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   546	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   547	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   548	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   550	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   552	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   553	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   554	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   555	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   556	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   557	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   558	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   559	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   560	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   561	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   562	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   564	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   566	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   567	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   568	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   569	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   570	          else true
   571	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   572	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   573	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   574	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   575	          else true
   576	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   577	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   578	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   579	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   580	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   581	    else false
   582	
   583	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   584	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   585	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   586	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   587	-/
   588	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   589	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   590	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   591	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   592	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   593	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   594	  μ_prob := by sorry
   595	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   596	
   597	end
   598	
   599	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290

   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   299	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.

   301	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=

   304	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   305	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   306	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   307	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   309	-/
   310	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   311	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   312	
   313	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   314	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   315	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   316	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).

   318	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   319	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩

   321	
   322	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   323	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   324	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.

   330	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   331	    exact
   332	      Distribution.map

   334	        (fun s =>
   335	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   336	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))

   632		constant size, so each subtest of the win predicate
   633		(Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}) is executed with probability
   634		bounded below by a universal constant.

   636		and~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} then follow directly from the
   637		corresponding subtests and the assumption that $\mathcal{S}$ succeeds

   639		from the consistency subtest of the low individual degree game executed

   642		of the line-versus-point clauses
   643		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}, invoked by the low-degree
   644		check of Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}). An outcome pair
   645		$(a,b)$ with $a \neq b$ in $\F_q$ is a line answer evaluating at $u$
   646		to $a$ against the point answer $b$, which the clause rejects; a pair
   647		$(\bot,b)$ is a line answer with no evaluation at $u$, which the
   648		universally quantified clause rejects against every point answer $b$

   650		Remark~\ref{rem:deg-line-representatives}); and the pairs $(a,\bot)$
   651		contribute no mass, since the class

   654		unless the sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting, and those underlying
   655		items~\ref{enu:qld-ms} and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} accept vacuously
   656		unless $\omega$ is anticommuting. Since the parameter tuple $(q,m,d)$
   657		is admissible (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), $m$ divides $q$, so
   658		$1 \leq m \leq q$, and Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} shows that

   660		least $\frac12$ and anticommuting with probability at least $2^{-4}$.

   662		probability of the corresponding subtest by a factor of at most $2^4$,

   664		and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} follow from the corresponding subtests.

   666		check is executed with constant probability over the choice of a pair

   668		$2^{-4}$. Finally, that all approximations
   669		also hold with $\approx_\eps$ in place of $\simeq_\eps$ is immediate
   670		from Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}.

   159	\begin{lemma}[Probability of anticommuting tuples]
   160		\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
   161		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb, MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_eq}
   162		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb, MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb_ge_half}
   163		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_ge_of_m_le_q}
   164		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_ge_of_one_le_md}
   165		\leanok
   166		% The source states this result in a `fact' environment; it is stated here
   167		% as a lemma, and the paper label is kept verbatim.
   168		% The exact value of the anticommuting probability and the constant lower
   169		% bounds under the hypothesis m <= q are additions relative to the source,
   170		% which asserts only the two bounds displayed at the end of the statement;
   171		% the source states those bounds without the hypothesis m, d >= 1, under
   172		% which alone they hold (see the remark following this lemma). The
   173		% unconditional constant bounds are what the proof of the lemma labelled
   174		% lem:qld-win-implications uses.
   175		\uses{def:anticommuting-tuple}
   176		A tuple $\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)$ sampled uniformly at random from
   177		$(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$ is anticommuting with probability exactly
   178		\[
   179			\big(1 - q^{-1}\big)^{m+1} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   180		\]
   181		and commuting with the complementary probability, which is at least
   182		$\frac12$. In particular, if $m \leq q$, then $\omega$ is anticommuting
   183		with probability at least $2^{-4}$ and commuting with probability at
   184		least $\frac12$. If $m, d \geq 1$, then the probability that $\omega$ is
   185		anticommuting is at least
   186		\[
   187			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big(1 - \frac{md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}
   188			\,\geq\, \Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   189		\]
   190		and the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least
   191		$\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
   192	\end{lemma}
   193	\begin{proof}
   194		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:indicator-vector, def:admissible-size, def:binary-representation, lem:downsize_field, lem:one}
   195		By the definition of the indicator vector
   196		(Definition~\ref{def:indicator-vector}), expanding the product over the
   197		coordinates $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ into a sum over $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   198		gives
   199		\[
   200			\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)
   201			\,=\, \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_X)\, \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_Z)
   202			\,=\, \prod_{i=1}^{m} \big( u_{X,i}\, u_{Z,i} + (1 - u_{X,i})(1 - u_{Z,i}) \big)\,,
   203		\]
   204		and since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$, the $i$-th factor equals
   205		$1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$. Hence
   206		\[
   207			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\Big( (r_X r_Z) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}) \Big)\,.
   208		\]
   209		For any fixed $u_X$, the $m$ factors $1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$ are
   210		independent and uniformly distributed in $\F_q$ over the choice of
   211		$u_Z$, so all of them are nonzero with probability $(1-q^{-1})^m$;
   212		independently, $r_X \neq 0$ with probability $1 - q^{-1}$. If $r_X = 0$
   213		or some factor vanishes, then $\gamma(\omega) = 0$. Otherwise, over the
   214		uniform choice of $r_Z$, the argument of the trace is a uniformly random
   215		element of $\F_q$. Since $q = 2^k$ is admissible, the trace of an
   216		element of $\F_q$ equals the coordinate sum of its binary
   217		representation: writing $\kappa$ for the binary representation with
   218		respect to the fixed self-dual normal basis
   219		(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), item~2 of
   220		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   221		$\tr(c) = \tr(c \cdot 1) = \kappa(c) \cdot \kappa(1)$, and $\kappa(1)$
   222		is the all-ones vector by Lemma~\ref{lem:one}. As $\kappa$ is a
   223		bijection onto $\F_2^k$, a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace
   224		$0$ with probability exactly $\frac12$. Combining, the probability that
   225		$\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$ is exactly $(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \cdot \frac12$, and
   226		the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is the complement, which is
   227		at least $\frac12$.
   228	
   229		If $m \leq q$, then
   230		$(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \geq (1-q^{-1})^{q+1} = (1-q^{-1})^{q} \cdot (1-q^{-1})$,
   231		a product of two positive functions of $q$ that are nondecreasing for
   232		$q \geq 2$, so it is minimized at $q = 2$, where it equals $2^{-3}$;
   233		hence the anticommuting probability is at least $2^{-4}$.
   234	
   235		Finally, suppose $m, d \geq 1$, and consider the first inequality of
   236		the display, which bounds the anticommuting probability from below.
   237		If $md > q$, that lower bound is negative --- it is the product of
   238		the positive factors $1 - q^{-m}$, $1 - q^{-1}$, and $\frac12$ with
   239		the negative factor $1 - md/q$ --- so the anticommuting probability,
   240		being nonnegative, exceeds it. If $md \leq q$, then by Bernoulli's
   241		inequality
   242		$(1-q^{-1})^{m} \geq 1 - m/q \geq 1 - md/q \geq (1-q^{-m})(1-md/q)$,
   243		where the last step multiplies the nonnegative quantity $1 - md/q$
   244		by $1 - q^{-m} \leq 1$; multiplying by $1 - q^{-1}$ shows that the
   245		anticommuting probability is at least the first displayed bound. For
   246		the second inequality of the display, expanding the product shows
   247		that $(1-q^{-m})(1-q^{-1})(1-md/q)$ exceeds
   248		$1 - q^{-m} - q^{-1} - md/q$ by
   249		$q^{-m-1} + \frac{md}{q} \big( q^{-m} + q^{-1} - q^{-m-1} \big)$,
   250		a sum of nonnegative terms whatever the sign of $1 - md/q$; since
   251		$md \geq 1$ gives $q^{-m} \leq q^{-1} \leq md/q$, the product is
   252		therefore at least $1 - 3md/q$.
   253		The commuting probability is at least
   254		$\frac12 \geq \big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac12$.
   255	\end{proof}

   257	\begin{remark}[Source correction: the anticommuting probability]
   258		\label{rem:omega-anticomm-prob-correction}
   259		In the source, the statement corresponding to
   260		Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} asserts only the two bounds of the
   261		final display, without the hypothesis $m, d \geq 1$, and its proof
   262		begins with the claims that $\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)$ vanishes if and only
   263		if $u_X = 0$ and that $u_X = 0$ forces $\omega$ to be commuting. Both
   264		claims are incorrect: the coordinates of $\mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ sum to $1$
   265		for every $u \in \F_q^m$, so $\mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ never vanishes, and for
   266		$(q,m,d) = (2,1,0)$ the tuple $\omega = (0,0,1,1)$ is anticommuting.
   267		For $d = 0$ the bounds themselves fail: with $(q,m,d) = (2,1,0)$ ---
   268		a tuple with admissible field size and $m \mid q$, excluded from
   269		Definition~\ref{def:admissible} only by the requirement $d \geq 1$
   270		that the source leaves implicit --- the exact anticommuting
   271		probability
   272		$(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \cdot \frac12 = \frac18$ is smaller than the claimed
   273		lower bound $\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac12 = \frac12$. The
   274		proof given above therefore computes the probability exactly, using the
   275		characteristic-two product formula for
   276		$\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)$, in place of the
   277		source's argument via the Schwartz--Zippel lemma; the exact value also
   278		supplies the unconditional constant lower bounds used in the proof of
   279		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}.
   280	\end{remark}

   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two

   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.

    16	
    17	\section{At a glance}
    18	
    19	\begin{itemize}
    20	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The paper's global polynomial shorthand
    21	  couples two constants in a way that excludes a square-root function used
    22	  explicitly later in the same paper.
    23	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The formal correction is one predicate with
    24	  separate prefactor and exponent witnesses; no theorem statement changes.
    25	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The obstruction is elementary real
    26	  analysis.  Mathlib's real-power API will discharge concrete downstream
    27	  witnesses, while the corrected convention is project-local.
    28	  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs.} The downstream witnesses use the
    29	  \path{Real.rpow} API.  The obstruction here is the elementary fact that no
    30	  constant $C>0$ can bound $\sqrt{x}$ by $C x^C$ for every $x>0$.
    31	\end{itemize}
    32	
    33	\section{Key theorem forms}
    34	
    35	The paper's shorthand asks for one universal constant $C>0$ such that
    36	\[
    37	  f(x) \leq Cx^C \qquad (x>0).
    38	\]
    39	The formal one-parameter convention instead asks for constants $A\geq1$ and
    40	$r>0$ such that
    41	\[
    42	  0\leq f(x)\leq Ax^r \qquad (x\geq0).
    43	\]
    44	This form includes $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ by taking $A=1$ and $r=1/2$.
    45	
    46	\section{The source convention}
    47	
    48	The asymptotic conventions of \cite[lines~23--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} define
    49	$f(x)=\operatorname{poly}(x)$ using the same constant as prefactor and
    50	exponent.  Later, the Pauli basis analysis explicitly obtains
    51	$\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}(\eps)=\sqrt{\eps}$ and
    52	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt{\eps}$ at lines~508--520 and 649--676 of
    53	the chapter-14 source mirror.\footnote{The corresponding files are
    54	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex} and
    55	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.  The
    56	formal correction is tracked in
    57	\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}
    58	and descends from \localissue{0002}.}
    59	
    60	The coupled-constant inequality cannot hold for $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$.  At $x=1$ it
    61	would imply $C\geq1$.  For such a constant,
    62	\[
    63	  \frac{\sqrt{x}}{Cx^C}=C^{-1}x^{1/2-C}
    64	\]
    65	is unbounded as $x$ decreases to zero, contradicting the proposed inequality
    66	on all positive inputs.
    67	
    68	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
    69	
    70	The blueprint records only the paper's local assertions that the relevant
    71	errors are polynomial in $\eps$; those assertions include the displayed
    72	square-root choices.  The formal helper therefore separates the prefactor and
    73	exponent.\footnote{The helper is \leanid{IsPolyErr} in
    74	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/ErrorFunctions.lean}.}  This changes no
    75	source-labelled theorem and preserves the intended meaning that the error
    76	decays as a positive power of its argument.
    77	
    78	\section{Conclusion}
    79	
    80	The single-constant shorthand is incompatible with the paper's own
    81	square-root error functions.  Using independent positive exponent and
    82	prefactor witnesses is a local correction to that shorthand, not an
    83	unfaithful theorem dependency.

    38		\label{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}

    45		Given integers $d, m \geq 0$ and a prime power $q$, denote by
    46		$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables over
    47		$\F_q$ with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When
    48		the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when
    49		the number of variables is also clear from context, $\mathrm{ideg}_d$. We
    50		denote by $\deg_d$ the set of polynomials with \emph{total} degree at
    51		most $d$.
    52		% The line-restricted classes below are introduced only implicitly in the
    53		% source, in the statement of the lemma labelled lem:qld-comm-line-cons,
    54		% which reads them as polynomials "defined on the line". The coefficient
    55		% reading adopted here follows the answer format of the decision procedure
    56		% of the low individual degree game (source figure fig:ld-decider) and the
    57		% representative convention of def:polyfunc; see the remark following this
    58		% definition.
    59		For a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) presented
    60		by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
    61		question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
    62		point is the canonical representative of
    63		Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
    64		we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
    65		at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
    66		by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
    67		as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
    68		line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
    69		$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
    70		$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
    71		zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
    72		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
    73		\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
    74		every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
    75		unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,

    77		function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An

    81		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when

    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- A formalization-only identity used to construct canonical line
    33	descriptions: applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has
    34	the same effect as applying it once. -/
    35	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    36	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    37	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    38	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    39	
    40	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    41	inductive LineKind where
    42	  | axis
    43	  | diagonal
    44	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    45	
    46	/-- A seed-bearing line description for `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    47	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper
    48	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
    49	
    50	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    51	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    52	Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
    54	corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by

   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Multivariate polynomials in `m` variables whose total degree is at most
   110	`d`. This is the class `deg_d` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, blueprint
   111	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-48`, paper
   112	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-52`. -/
   113	abbrev TotalDegreePoly (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :=
   114	  {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K // p.totalDegree ≤ d}
   115	
   116	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   117	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   118	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   119	
   120	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   121	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   122	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   123	  fun i =>
   124	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   125	
   126	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   127	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   128	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   129	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   130	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   131	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   132	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   133	
   134	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   135	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   136	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   138	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   139	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   140	  classical
   141	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   142	    some (Classical.choose h)
   143	  else none
   144	
   145	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   147	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   151	
   152	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   153	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   154	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   156	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   157	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   158	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   159	      intro j hj
   160	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   161	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   162	
   163	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   164	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   165	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   171	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   172	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   173	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   174	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   175	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   176	
   177	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   178	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   179	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   180	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   181	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   182	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   183	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   184	
   185	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   186	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   187	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   188	  sorry
   189	
   190	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   191	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   192	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   193	  sorry
   194	
   195	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   196	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   197	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   198	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   199	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   200	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   201	
   202	end

   548	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>

    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=

     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
   196	
   197	[#1145]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/1145

## Blueprint Structure
- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.
- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`
- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`

## Lean Blueprint Macros
- `\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration
- `\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see "Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`" below
- `\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph
- `\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)
- `\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)

### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`

`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.

**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.

**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).

A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.

Excerpt from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`:

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Commutativity of the point measurements]\label{thm:commutativity-points}
  \lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.CommutativityPoints.commutativityPoints}
  \leanok
  \uses{def:good-strategy, def:approx_delta}
  Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$.
\end{proof}
```

**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

`leanblueprint` does not use distinct macro names for these two claims, so audits must distinguish them by environment context rather than by raw `\leanok` counts. A future split such as `\leanokstmt` / `\leanokproof` could make that distinction explicit, but that is only a possible later cleanup; the current convention is to keep `\leanok` and rely on placement.

A recurring historical example is the chapter 4 `Q/X/\widehat X/P` witness
layer.  Once Lean has construction theorems deriving the displayed identities
and estimates from the rank-reduction, sigma-range, positive-Gram, native
spectral-theorem, or rectangular-SVD hypotheses, the corresponding blueprint
entries may carry `\leanok`.  A declaration that merely projects an identity
from an opaque data record is not enough by itself, and a theorem depending on
extra rectangular-SVD data should not be used as evidence for an unconditional
paper statement unless a separate construction supplies that data.

## Dependency Graph Colors (web)
- **Light green box**: definition with `\lean` + `\leanok` (defined in Lean)
- **Green**: theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with `\lean` + statement-level `\leanok` (statement matched in Lean)
- **Dark green**: either (i) theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with both statement-level and proof-level `\leanok` (fully formalized in Lean), or (ii) a `\mathlibok` node
- **Blue**: ready to state/prove (all deps are done)

   375		\hat{W}^r(u) = W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))\;,

   379	For $a\in \F_q$ define corresponding projections
   380	\[
   381		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a = \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\;.
   382	\]
   383	Note that $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ can be equivalently
   384	written as a sum of projectors by applying Fourier
   385	identities. Specifically, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^{m}$, and
   386	$a \in \F_q$, define the projector
   387	\begin{equation} \tau^{W, u}_{a} =
   388	  \tau^{W}_{[ g_{\cdot}(u) = a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits}: h
   389	    \cdot \ind_m(u) = a} \tau^{W}_{h}\;. \label{eq:qld-point-obs-def} \end{equation}

   391	\begin{align*}
   392	  \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a
   393	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \,
   394	    W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r
   395	    \cdot \ind_m(u)) \\
   396	    &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   397	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   398	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   399	    \sum_{h \in \F_q^n}
   400	    (-1)^{\tr( r( h \cdot \ind_m(u)))} \tau^{W}_{h} \Big) \\
   401	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   402	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   403	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   404	    \sum_{a'' \in \F_q}
   405	    (-1)^{\tr(a'' r)} \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big) \\
   406	  &=	\sum_{a',a'' \in \F_q} \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr((a + a' + a'')r)} \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \\
   407	  &= \sum_{\substack{a',a'' \in \F_q \\ a' + a'' = a}}  \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''}\;,
   408	\end{align*}

   410	first tensor factor and \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj} on the second, and in the third line we
   411	have used \Cref{eq:qld-point-obs-def}.

   413	\begin{equation}

   416	\end{equation}

   418	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-22}
   419	\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \frac{1}{2} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{W}^r(u) \Big)\;.

   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.
   461

    81		\begin{align*}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}

   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

   523	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}
   524	There exists a function $\delta_{\Line}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
   525		For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and lines $\line$ there exists a projective measurement $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f \}_{f \in \deg_{md}(\line)}$, acting on registers $\alice\alice'$ or $\bob\alice''$, such that:
   526		\begin{enumerate}
   527			\item  (\textbf{Self-consistency})\label{enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons}  For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $r \in \F_q$, on average over a uniformly random  pair $(\line, u)$
   528	                drawn from the line-point distribution
   529	                (\Cref{def:line-point-dist}),
   530			\[
   531				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   532			\]
   533			
   534			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements I}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}
   535			On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
   536	                drawn from the line-point distribution, 
   537			\[
   538				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{f(u)})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   539			\]		
   540			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements II}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   541			On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
   542	                drawn from the line-point distribution,
   543			\[
   544				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line}  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   545			\]
   546	              \end{enumerate}
   547	                    Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
   548	      also hold.
   549	\end{lemma}

   551	\begin{proof}
   552		Define the operator
   553		\[
   554			\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f = \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' = f}} M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''}\;,
   555		\]
   556		where the Pauli operator $\tau^{W,\line}_{f''}$ acting on register $\alice'$ is obtained by measuring all $\nqubits$ qudits in the basis $W$ to obtain an outcome $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and then returning the restriction $f''$ of $g_h: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ to the line $\line$. Here, $g_h$ is the degree-$d$ low-degree extension of $h$ defined in~\eqref{eq:ld-encoding}. 
   557

   559	
   560	\Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}, the consistency with the points measurements, follows because on average over $(\line,u)$ drawn from the line-point distribution we have
   561	\begin{align}
   562		&(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \\
   563		&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   564	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   565	  \alice'} \\
   566	        &= \sum_{\substack{f', f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line): \\ f' + f'' =
   567	  f}} ((M^{(\Line, W), \line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W, \line}_{f''})
   568	  \cdot (M^{(\Line, W), \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = f'(u)]} )_{\alice
   569	  \alice'} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-1} \\
   570		&\approx_\eps \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\
   571	  f' + f'' = f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes
   572	  \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes
   573	  (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{f'(u)})_{\bob
   574	  \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-2} \\
   575	  	&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   576	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   577	  \alice'} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{f'(u)} \otimes
   578	  \tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-3} \\
   579		&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   580	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   581	  \alice'} \otimes \Big (\sum_{\substack{a', a'' : \\ a' + a'' = f'(u)
   582	  + f''(u)}}  M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'} \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big
   583	  )_{\bob \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-4} \\
   584		&= (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes
   585	   (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{f(u)})_{\bob \alice''}\;. \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons-eps}
   586	\end{align}
   587	\Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-1} follows from the projectivity of
   588	$\{\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_{f}\}$. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-2} follows from the consistency between the line
   589	and point measurements (\Cref{enu:qld-ld} in
   590	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}) together with
   591	\Cref{fact:add-a-proj2}. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-3}
   592	follows from the exact consistency between the $\{ \tau^{W,\line}_{f''} \}$ and $\{
   593	\tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)} \}$ measurements on the $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ registers. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-4} follows because
   594	the consistency of the $\tau$ measurements force $a' = f'(u)$ and $a''
   595	= f''(u)$ . This establishes \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}, with
   596	approximation error $\eps$.
   597	
   598	To show \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} we would like to first
   599	apply~\Cref{fact:data-processing} to \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons-eps},
   600	to sum over all functions $f$ that evaluate to the same value at a given
   601	point $u$. Unfortunately, we cannot use the Fact as written, since the
   602	bound in \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons} is in terms of $\approx$, not
   603	$\simeq$, and moreover the right-hand side does not have the form $I
   604	\ot B$. Instead, we show the desired bound by direct calculation from \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons-eps}
   605	\begin{align}
   606	  \eps &\geq \E_{\omega} \sum_{f} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   607	  \line}_f )^2 \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{f(u)})^2 \ket{\hat{\psi}}
   608	  \\
   609	                 &= \E_{\omega} \sum_{f} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   610	                   \line}_f  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{f(u)})
   611	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
   612	                 &= \E_{\omega} \sum_{a} \sum_{f: f(u) = a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   613	                   \line}_f  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})
   614	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
   615	                 &=\E_{\omega} \sum_{a}  \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   616	                   \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]}  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})
   617	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}},
   618	\end{align}
   619	where in going to the second line we have used the projectivity of the
   620	measurements $\{\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_f\}$ and
   621	$\{\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}\}$.
   622	Thus, we have deduced that
   623	\begin{equation}
   624	\label{eq:qld-comm-line-1}
   625	(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\eps (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   626	\end{equation}
   627	Since both the $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f\}$ and $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a \}$ measurements are projective, we also get 
   628	\begin{align}
   629	\Id &= \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   630	      a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes I_{\bob \alice''}\notag\\
   631	&= \sum_a \Big((\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   632	                                                               a]})_{\alice
   633	                                                               \alice'}
   634	                                                               \ot
   635	                                                               I_{\bob
   636	                                                               \alice''}-(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\Big) \notag\\
   637	&\qquad\qquad + \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.\label{eq:com-1a}
   638	\end{align}
   639	For projective sub-measurements $\{A_i\}$ and $\{B_i\}$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$,
   640	\begin{align*}
   641	\sum_i \bra{\varphi}\big(A_i-B_i\big)\ket{\varphi} &= \sum_i \bra{\varphi}A_i(A_i-B_i)\ket{\varphi} + \sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)B_i\ket{\varphi}\\
   642	&\leq \Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}A_i^2\ket{\varphi} \Big)^{1/2}\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2\ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2} \\
   643	&\qquad\qquad+ \Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2 \ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}B_i^2\ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\\
   644	&\leq 2\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2 \ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\;.
   645	\end{align*}
   646	Applying this fact to the projective sub-measurements $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'}\}_a$ and $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:com-1a} and using~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-1} gives
   647	\begin{equation}
   648	\label{eq:qld-comm-line-2}
   649		\Id \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   650	      \end{equation}
   651	      To go from~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} to \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} of the lemma we use another fact about
   652	      projective measurements. For families of projective measurements $\{A^x_i\}$
   653	      and $\{B^x_i\}$ acting on separate registers of a bipartite state
   654	      $\ket{\phi}$, suppose $I \approx_{\delta} \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i$. Then
   655	      \begin{align*}
   656	        \delta &\geq \E_{x} \Big\| \Big(\Id - \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i\Big) \ket{\phi}\Big\|^2  \\
   657	               &= \E_{x} \Big(1 + \bra{\phi} \Big(\sum_i A^x_i \ot
   658	                 B^x_i\Big)^2 \ket{\phi} - 2 \sum_i \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_i
   659	                 \ket{\phi} \Big) \\
   660	               &= 1 - \E_{x} \sum_i \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_i \ket{\phi}\;,
   661	\end{align*}
   662	      where we used the projectivity in going from the second to
   663	      the third line, to remove the square. Thus
   664	      \[ \E_{x} \sum_{i \neq j} \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_j \ket{\phi} \leq
   665	        \delta\;, \]
   666	      and $A^x_i \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_i$. By
   667	      Item~1 of \Cref{fact:agreement}, this in turn implies that $A^x_i \ot I
   668	      \approx_\delta I \ot B^x_i$. Applying this fact to the projective
   669	      measurements $\{ (\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   670	        a]})_{\alice \alice'} \}_a$ and $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),
   671	        u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} gives
   672	      \[
   673		(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}.
   674	      \]
   675	      Taking the function $\delta_{\Line}$ in the lemma to be $\sqrt{\eps}$,
   676	      this yields the conclusion of \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   677	      of the lemma.
   678	\end{proof}

  1294		$\Id \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \sum_a \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} \ot \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$.
  1295		A second elementary fact about projective measurements --- if
  1296		$\Id \approx_\delta \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i$ for families of projective
  1297		measurements $\{A^x_i\}$ and $\{B^x_i\}$ acting on separate registers
  1298		of a bipartite state, then $A^x_i \ot \Id \simeq_\delta \Id \ot B^x_i$,
  1299		and hence $A^x_i \ot \Id \approx_\delta \Id \ot B^x_i$ by item~1 of
  1300		Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} --- is then applied to the two families
  1301		completed as in Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}: the
  1302		evaluation classes of the expanded line measurement together with
  1303		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$,
  1304		and the expanded point measurement together with
  1305		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\bot} = 0$. Both completed families
  1306		are projective measurements, and the completion leaves the sum in the
  1307		hypothesis unchanged, since the term for the outcome $\bot$ vanishes.
  1308		Restricted to the outcomes in $\F_q$, the conclusion yields
  1309		item~\ref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} with error $\sqrt{\eps}$, so that
  1310		$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps) = \sqrt{\eps}$. The symmetric
  1311		equivalents follow from
  1312		Lemma~\ref{lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer}.
  1313	\end{proof}
  1314	
  1315	The expanded point and line measurements constructed in this section, being
  1316	approximately consistent and approximately commuting, are combined into a
  1317	single strategy for the classical low individual degree test in
  1318	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining}.
